IONIX_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional severity floor applied client-side on the findings surface. Accepts the canonical Faraday enum (info / low / medium / high / critical) plus Ionix-side aliases (Important / Major / Moderate / Informational / Negligible / Sev1..Sev5 / P1..P5). Defaults to '' (no filter; we emit the full hits surface). Garbage values are logged and ignored.

IONIX_STATUS.description: Optional finding status filter forwarded to Ionix as the status query param on /api/v1/findings, and enforced again client-side as a defensive belt + braces. Accepts the canonical Faraday enum (open / closed / risk-accepted) plus the Ionix-side aliases (new / active / in_progress / investigating / triaged -> open; resolved / remediated / fixed / mitigated / patched -> closed; false_positive / wont_fix / dismissed -> risk-accepted). Defaults to '' (no filter; Ionix returns every finding regardless of status). Garbage values are logged and ignored.

IONIX_PAGES.description: Optional per-surface page-walk cap. Each Ionix v1 search page returns up to 100 hits via limit=100; IONIX_PAGES bounds the offset walk so a stray operator filter can't fan out into 100k+ requests against the rate-limited Ionix API. Numeric / numeric-string input accepted; floats are floored. Clamped to [1, 50]. Defaults to 5 (~ 500 hits per surface, 1000 total across assets + findings).

name: ionix
title: Ionix
description: Ionix EASM importer. Pulls externally-discovered assets and findings from the Ionix REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Each Ionix asset becomes one Faraday host (ip = the asset's first public IP, falling back to synthetic 0.0.0.0 for domain-keyed assets); per-asset findings attach as one Faraday vulnerability per finding_id with the [EASM] engine prefix. Endpoints used: GET /api/v1/assets (paginated external-asset inventory; the canonical Ionix pivot - every finding joins by asset_id) and GET /api/v1/findings (paginated finding inventory with severity + category + cves + remediation guidance; query string also carries the operator-supplied status floor so Ionix narrows server-side). Pagination is offset-based: limit=100 per page, offset advanced via the response envelope's next_offset cursor (or current_offset + page_size when the envelope is silent), walked page-by-page until the page comes up short or IONIX_PAGES is reached. Severity bucketing walks the string severity field first (Critical / High / Medium / Low / Info) and falls back to priority / risk_rating / risk_score (Ionix 0-10 scale) then CVSS when nothing else lands; aliases collapse Ionix-side labels (Important / Major / Moderate / Informational / Negligible / Sev1..Sev5 / P1..P5) onto the canonical Faraday bucket. Status mapping covers new / in_progress / investigating / triaged -> open, resolved / closed / remediated / fixed / mitigated / patched -> closed, and false_positive / risk_accepted / accepted_risk / wont_fix -> risk-accepted. Refs include Ionix-Asset / Ionix-AssetName / Ionix-AssetType / Ionix-Tenant / Ionix-Id / Ionix-Category / Ionix-Port pivots plus any url / reference_url / evidence_url surfaced on the finding. Auth: Ionix uses a single long-lived API key created in the Ionix console under Settings -> API Keys -> New. The dispatcher carries the key on every request as the Authorization: Bearer <IONIX_API_KEY> header. IONIX_HOST is the Ionix tenant host (e.g. api.ionix.io); service-account keys carry the tenant scope so no workspace param is required. Tags: [ionix, easm].
